brief: Tariff-driven inflation, oil near $106/bbl, US fiscal concerns, and competition for AI funding are pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.99%, close to levels last seen before the 2008 financial crisis. Every S&P 500 sector except energy is lower as markets turn risk-off ahead of the FOMC (Wednesday), BoE (Thursday), and BOJ (Friday). Markets price a 90% chance the Fed hikes this week; Mericle expects a hike. Goldman Sachs sees no fundamental case for a hike but thinks the Fed may feel bound by that pricing; it still expects the bull market to hold because earnings remain strong despite higher rates. The September Empire Manufacturing survey missed expectations: new orders and shipments weakened sharply since August, employment ticked up slightly, and both current and expected prices-paid components rose. Separately, Goldman's credit team reports year-to-date foreign purchases of US corporate bonds at $251bn through June, on pace to rival 2025's $392bn record, and expects a floor under foreign flows with broad repatriation unlikely. Conference notes: AeroVironment reiterated FY27 guidance (10% yoy, 86% visibility) with added conservatism for budget timing; TE Connectivity cited datacenter, energy, and defense growth against a muted automotive market; retail conference presenters called consumers resilient but selective.
